what_it_measures: Number of reads (both mates counted) left after fastp filtering. For paired data, 100,000 reads is 50,000 pairs.
how_to_read_it: Below the fail floor there is too little data to assess the sample at all. Above it, whether the depth is enough depends on genome size.
caveat: Depth of coverage needs a genome size, which v0.1 does not have. These are sanity floors, not adequacy thresholds.

what_it_measures: Fraction of bases with Phred quality 30 or above (an estimated error rate of 1 in 1000 or better).
how_to_read_it: Most modern Illumina runs exceed 0.80 after trimming. A low value points to a run or library problem rather than biology.
caveat: Expected values differ by instrument and read length. Longer reads (2x250, 2x300) usually score lower than 2x150.
provenance: adapted from R_Bible Part 16.2 (Q30+ across most of the read); numeric cut-offs are provisional pipeline defaults

what_it_measures: Fraction of input reads that survived fastp's quality, length and N-content filters.
how_to_read_it: A large loss means many reads were too short or too poor after trimming. Check the per-base quality and adapter content.
caveat: Aggressive trimming settings remove more reads. R_Bible Part 16.2 warns that over-trimming has a real cost.

what_it_measures: Estimated fraction of reads that are duplicates of another read.
how_to_read_it: High duplication can be PCR artefact or low library complexity. A single outlier sample in a batch is more suspicious than a uniformly high batch.
caveat: Amplicon data is expected to be highly duplicated, so this warning does not apply there. A dominant organism in a metagenome can also cause real duplication. Never a fail on its own.
provenance: adapted from R_Bible Part 16.2 (duplication level); cut-off is a provisional pipeline default

what_it_measures: Fraction of reads in which fastp found and removed adapter sequence.
how_to_read_it: Adapters are removed, so this is not a failure. A high value means many inserts were shorter than the read length.
caveat: Expected to be high for short-insert libraries (some amplicon and degraded-DNA preps).
provenance: adapted from R_Bible Part 16.2 (adapter content); cut-off is a provisional pipeline default

what_it_measures: Fraction of bases that are G or C.
how_to_read_it: Compare against the expected GC for the organism. A bimodal GC distribution in the FastQC report suggests contamination or two very different organisms.
caveat: No threshold: expected GC is species-specific and v0.1 does not know the species.
provenance: adapted from R_Bible Parts 16.2 and 18.4 (GC content)

what_it_measures: Most common distance between the outer ends of a read pair, estimated from read overlap.
how_to_read_it: Informational. A peak shorter than the read length means mates overlap heavily and adapters were read into.
caveat: Paired-end only. fastp can only estimate inserts short enough for the mates to overlap.

what_it_measures: Mean length of read 1 after trimming.
how_to_read_it: Informational. A large drop from the raw read length means heavy trimming.
caveat: Reported for read 1. Read 2 is usually similar but slightly shorter.

what_it_measures: Number of reads in the file.
how_to_read_it: Below the fail floor there is too little data to assess the sample at all.
caveat: Sanity floor only. Whether the data is sufficient depends on genome size and read length, and v0.1 does not have the genome size.

how_to_read_it: Divide by the expected genome size to estimate depth of coverage, e.g. 500 Mb over a 5 Mb genome is about 100x.
caveat: No threshold: adequacy depends on genome size, which v0.1 does not have.

what_it_measures: Read length N50: half of all sequenced bases are in reads at least this long.
how_to_read_it: Longer reads span repeats such as rRNA operons (about 5 kb), which is what makes closed assemblies possible. Under 1 kb is unusual for ONT and suggests degraded DNA or a mislabelled platform.
caveat: This is READ N50, not assembly N50. R_Bible Part 18.4's guidance (> 100 kb good) is for assembly contigs and does not apply here. Rapid kits give shorter reads than ligation kits.

what_it_measures: Mean read quality, averaged over error probabilities and then converted back to a Phred score.
how_to_read_it: Below about Q7 is below the default pass filter of every MinKNOW basecalling model, which suggests failed or unfiltered reads.
caveat: Averaging error probabilities gives a LOWER value than naively averaging Q scores, so this will not match tools that do the latter. Modern R10.4.1 chemistry with high-accuracy basecalling usually exceeds Q15.

how_to_read_it: Informational. Much lower than the N50 means many short reads alongside a smaller number of long ones.
caveat: Read-count based, unlike N50, which is base weighted.
